ai.title: Switch tool renderers from bgBlack to gray
ai.summary: Replaced `bgBlack` with `gray` in `npm-app/src/utils/tool-renderers.ts` for tool call and parameter output. This improves readability across various terminal color schemes by removing the black background block. The change affects default renderers and specific tool handlers like `read_files` and `edit_file`.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs a tool like reading or editing a file, it prints a small header and some details about what it's doing. Those printed blocks used to have a solid black background, which made the text hard to read in many terminal color schemes. Now they use a gray color instead of a black background, so the text stays readable across different themes. If you watch the assistant run a tool today, you'll see gray text where there used to be a black block, no other behavior changed.

ai.title: Add cargo check example to terminal command classifier prompt
ai.summary: Added 'run cargo check' to the non-terminal command examples in `backend/src/check-terminal-command.ts`. This clarifies that natural language instructions to run commands should not be classified as terminal commands themselves. Internal prompt tuning only.

eli5.text: The instructions that govern how the assistant decides whether something is a command to run or just a request have been clarified with one extra example: telling it to "run cargo check" is now treated as a plain-language request (the words "run cargo check"), not as a command the assistant should execute on its own. This affects only how the assistant interprets your prompts behind the scenes, so you won't see anything new on your screen; the assistant will already handle this case the way it was intended to.

ai.title: main-prompt: add direct answer instruction
ai.summary: Added 'If the user asks a question, simply answer the question rather than making changes to the code' to the core instructions in backend/src/main-prompt.ts. This ensures the agent prioritizes answering queries over modifying code. Scope limited to backend prompt logic.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a question, it will now give you a straight answer instead of automatically trying to edit code. This only affects how the assistant responds to questions, not how it performs actual coding tasks. The change is live today and applies to the assistant's core instructions that guide its behavior.

ai.title: claude.md added as knowledge file
ai.summary: claude.md files are now recognized as knowledge files alongside knowledge.md. Backend prompts and npm-app file filtering logic updated to include claude.md suffix. This expands the context sources for the AI agent without requiring manual configuration changes.

eli5.text: As you work with the coding assistant, it can now read a project instruction file named claude.md in addition to the usual knowledge.md file, so more of your project's custom setup and notes get automatically considered without you having to point them out each time. This works everywhere the assistant is used today.

ai.title: Prompt allows dev server start on explicit request
ai.summary: main-prompt.ts and tools.ts updated to permit starting dev servers only when explicitly requested. Previous logic strictly forbade it without user initiation. Scope limited to backend prompt constants. Aligns safety guardrails with user intent.

eli5.text: The assistant is no longer allowed to start a development server on its own initiative. Previously, the system instructed the assistant to never start a dev server without the user asking, and now that same rule has been extended to git commands and scripts. This change is live today and affects you directly: if you ask the assistant to begin work that might involve running a server or script, you now need to explicitly request it rather than having the assistant offer or do it automatically.

ai.title: Version 1.0.226
ai.summary: Bumped version to 1.0.226 in npm-app/package.json. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: The app's version number was bumped from 1.0.225 to 1.0.226 as part of packaging this release. What you actually get by updating is a change to how billing works: debts and credits are now settled against each other in memory before your balance is shown. This means you won't be blocked from seeing a positive net balance just because you had a debt at some point. This is live today for anyone using the billing features.

ai.title: Case insensitive knowledge file matching
ai.summary: Project file detection now matches `knowledge.md` and `CLAUDE.md` case-insensitively. `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` lowercases paths before checking extensions. Prompt text in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/system-prompt/prompts.ts` updated to use uppercase `CLAUDE.md`.

eli5.text: The assistant now recognizes project instruction files regardless of whether they are named in uppercase or lowercase. Previously, a file named CLAUDE.md would be missed if your computer stored it as claude.md; the matching now treats both spellings as the same. If you create or rename these files with any casing, the assistant will still find and read them the next time it scans your project.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.227
ai.summary: Freebuff CLI package version incremented to 1.0.227. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The assistant software got a version-number label bump to keep package installs working correctly. If you look, you would not notice anything new or different; the program behaves exactly the same as before. The other improvements shipped with this release, like case-insensitive knowledge file matching, are separate from this bump.

ai.title: Add getToolCallString helper, fix xml-stream-parser test
ai.summary: Added `getToolCallString` to `common/src/constants/tools.ts` to generate XML-formatted tool call strings from tool names and parameters. The `postbuild` script in `npm-app/package.json` now copies `src/utils/__tests__/*.txt` fixtures to `dist/utils/__tests__/`, enabling `xml-stream-parser.test.ts` to run against built output. Added `strip-ansi` as a dev dependency to support test assertions.

eli5.text: If you ever looked at how the assistant formats requests to its own tools, there's now a small helper that builds those XML-style command strings consistently from a tool name and its parameters, so the same request always comes out the same way; otherwise, nothing looks different yet, since this is just an internal convenience that no feature actually calls today. Behind the scenes, the build step that packages the app was also taught to copy over a few text files that some of the stream-parsing tests depend on, plus one supporting library for cleaning up formatted text during assertions, which keeps that part of the test suite from breaking when run against the built product.

ai.title: Fix test imports and tool call generation
ai.summary: Corrects import paths in `string.test.ts` and `tool-renderers.test.ts` to resolve module resolution failures. Replaces hardcoded XML strings with `getToolCallString` helper in tool renderer tests to ensure consistent format generation. Updates ANSI stripping logic to use `strip-ansi` package and adjusts expected output trailing newlines.

eli5.text: Some behind-the-scenes testing code was updated to fix a few small glitches, which makes sure the system's built-in checks still run properly. These are test-only changes, so you won't see any difference in how the tool works, but it helps keep everything stable. Live today.

ai.title: Enforce parameter order in getToolCallString
ai.summary: Refactored `getToolCallString` in `common/src/constants/tools.ts` to enforce parameter ordering based on `toolSchema`. Backend files `main-prompt.ts` and `tools.ts` now use this helper for generating tool call strings instead of hardcoded templates. This ensures consistent XML-like tag structure for tools like `read_files` and `add_subgoal`.

eli5.text: When the assistant writes certain commands, it now follows a fixed order for the information inside each command, matching the order that each command type expects. This affects the assistant's internal text formatting and makes the output more consistent, but it does not change any feature you use directly. If you looked at the raw response text, the pieces of information within commands like reading files or updating goals would always appear in the same sequence.
